topics.title: Extent and Commencement of GST Law
topics.section: CGST Act Sec 1 & 2(56), IGST Act Sec 1, UTGST Act Sec 1
explain: CGST Act extends to the whole of India, including its territorial waters up to 12 nautical miles.
SGST Acts apply to all States and Union Territories with Legislature (Delhi, Puducherry, and Jammu & Kashmir).
UTGST Act applies to 6 Union Territories without Legislature: Andaman & Nicobar, Lakshadweep, Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu, Ladakh, Chandigarh, and Other Territory.
IGST Act applies across all of India for inter-State supplies and imports.

flow.title: Applicable GST Act Based on Supply Type
steps: Supply across State or UT borders

topics.example: A trader in Ladakh sells goods locally; CGST and UTGST are charged because Ladakh is a Union Territory without a Legislature.
remember: Delhi, Puducherry, and Jammu & Kashmir have legislatures and levy SGST, not UTGST.
India includes territorial waters up to 12 nautical miles and airspace above it.
mistakes: Confusing J&K, Delhi, and Puducherry as UTGST areas; they have legislatures and levy SGST.
Thinking IGST is an additional tax on top of CGST instead of a single combined tax.

quiz.q: Which Act applies along with CGST for an intra-State supply made in Chandigarh?
quiz.why: Chandigarh is a UT without legislature, so UTGST Act applies alongside the CGST Act.

quiz.q: Territorial waters of India extend up to how many nautical miles from the baseline?
quiz.why: Under Section 2(56) of CGST Act, territorial waters extend up to 12 nautical miles into the sea.

topics.title: Key Definitions under GST
explain: Goods means movable property other than money and securities, but includes actionable claims, growing crops, and grass.
Services means anything other than goods, money, and securities, but includes money conversion activities for separate consideration.
Taxable Person means any person who is registered or liable to be registered under Section 22 or Section 24.
Exempt Supply includes nil rate supplies, wholly exempt supplies, and non-taxable supplies.
Non-taxable Supply means a supply of goods or services not leviable to tax under CGST or IGST Act (e.g., alcoholic liquor for human consumption).
Aggregate Turnover includes taxable, exempt, export, and inter-State supplies under the same PAN, but excludes inward RCM supplies and GST taxes.

flow.title: Calculating Aggregate Turnover on All-India PAN Basis
steps: Add export of goods and services
Exclude CGST, SGST, UTGST, IGST, Cess

topics.example: A professional with one PAN running a consultancy (taxable) and a book printing business (exempt) must add both turnovers together to check registration threshold.
remember: Money and securities are neither goods nor services.
Aggregate turnover is calculated on an all-India basis for the same Permanent Account Number (PAN).
mistakes: Including inward supplies liable to RCM in the aggregate turnover calculation.
Including GST taxes and cesses while checking turnover threshold limits.

quiz.q: Which of the following is specifically included in the definition of 'goods' under Section 2(52)?
quiz.why: Goods includes actionable claims, growing crops, and grass, but excludes money and securities.

quiz.q: Aggregate turnover under Section 2(6) explicitly EXCLUDES which of the following items?
quiz.why: Inward supplies on which tax is payable under RCM are excluded from aggregate turnover.

topics.title: Levy and Collection of CGST & IGST
topics.section: CGST Act Sec 9, IGST Act Sec 5
explain: CGST is levied on intra-State supplies (maximum statutory rate is 20%).
IGST is levied on inter-State supplies (maximum statutory rate is 40%).
The taxable event triggering GST levy is 'Supply' of goods or services.
Alcoholic liquor for human consumption and un-denatured extra neutral alcohol (ENA) used for liquor manufacture are completely outside GST.
GST on 5 petroleum products (crude, petrol, diesel, natural gas, ATF) is deferred until a notified date.
Tax is paid via Forward Charge (supplier pays), Reverse Charge (recipient pays), or Electronic Commerce Operator (ECO pays).

flow.title: Determining Liability to Pay GST under Section 9
steps: Check if item is outside GST

topics.example: Selling alcoholic liquor for human consumption attracts State Excise duty, not GST, because it is constitutionally excluded from GST.
remember: Maximum CGST rate is 20%, so maximum combined IGST rate is 40%.
5 petroleum products remain outside GST levy until a future date is notified by the Government.
mistakes: Assuming petrol and diesel are exempt under GST; they are non-taxable pending notification.
Believing IGST maximum statutory cap is 20% instead of 40%.

quiz.q: What is the maximum statutory rate of CGST specified under Section 9(1)?
quiz.why: Section 9(1) caps CGST at 20% (making the combined IGST cap 40%).

quiz.q: Which product is completely outside the purview of GST law?
quiz.why: Alcoholic liquor for human consumption is constitutionally excluded from the purview of GST.

topics.title: Reverse Charge Mechanism (RCM)
topics.section: CGST Act Sec 9(3), 9(4), IGST Act Sec 5(3), 5(4)
explain: Under RCM, the statutory liability to pay GST and fulfill compliances shifts from supplier to recipient.
GTA services attract 5% RCM (no ITC) unless GTA opts for forward charge @ 5% or 18%. RCM does not apply to Govt entities registered only for TDS.
Legal services by advocates/firms to business entities in taxable territory are under RCM.
Sponsorship services to body corporate or partnership firm are under RCM.
Services by directors (sitting fees/remuneration outside employment contract) to companies are under RCM.
Renting of residential dwelling to a GST-registered person is under RCM.
Renting of commercial property by an unregistered person to a registered person (non-composition) is under RCM.

Other RCM services: Arbitral tribunal, Insurance/Recovery agents, Copyrights (music/artist), Individual DSAs, Security services (non-body corporate supplier), Renting of motor vehicle (fuel cost included, 5% rate, non-body corporate supplier to body corporate), Securities lending, Import of services.

flow.title: RCM Applicability Determination Process
steps: Check if service is notified under 9(3)
If RCM applies, recipient pays tax

topics.example: ABC Ltd. pays sitting fees to its independent director; ABC Ltd. must deposit GST under reverse charge mechanism.
remember: RCM applies on renting residential dwelling only if the tenant/recipient is a GST-registered person.
GTA services are under RCM at 5% unless the GTA opts to pay tax under forward charge.
mistakes: Applying RCM on director salary subjected to TDS under Section 192 (salary is Schedule III non-supply).
Applying RCM on security services supplied BY a body corporate (it is forward charge).

quiz.q: Who is liable to pay GST when an unregistered individual rents a commercial shop to a registered company (not under composition)?
quiz.why: Under Entry 5AB of RCM notification, renting of immovable property by an unregistered person to a registered person is under RCM.

quiz.q: If an author takes registration under GST and opts to pay tax under forward charge with proper invoice declaration, who pays GST?
quiz.why: Authors can opt out of RCM by taking registration, filing a declaration, and issuing invoices with the prescribed declaration.

topics.title: Tax Payable by Electronic Commerce Operator (ECO) under Section 9(5)
topics.section: CGST Act Sec 9(5), IGST Act Sec 5(5)
explain: For specific notified services supplied through an ECO, the ECO is deemed the supplier liable to pay GST.

Notified services: Passenger transport (radio-taxi, motorcab, motorcycle, omnibus except by company), Accommodation (hotels/inns unless supplier liable under 22(1)), House-keeping (unless supplier liable under 22(1)), Restaurant services (except at specified premises), Local delivery (unless supplier liable under 22(1)).
Specified premises means hotel accommodation with value of supply > Rs 7,500 per unit per day.
ECO must pay GST entirely in cash and cannot use Input Tax Credit (ITC) for Section 9(5) liabilities.
ECOs do not collect TCS under Section 52 on Section 9(5) notified services.

flow.title: Identifying Tax Paying Entity for ECO Notified Services
steps: Is ECO present in taxable territory?
If No representative -> Appoint local person

topics.example: When a customer orders food on Zomato from a local eatery, Zomato (ECO) collects and remits 5% GST directly to the Government.
remember: ECO cannot use ITC to pay GST liability on Section 9(5) notified services; payment must be in cash.
Restaurant services at specified premises (> Rs 7,500 room tariff) remain payable by the restaurant, not ECO.
mistakes: Assuming ECO collects TCS under Section 52 on Section 9(5) restaurant services.
Thinking accommodation service through ECO is always paid by ECO even if the hotel turnover exceeds registration limit.

quiz.q: Who is liable to pay GST on restaurant services provided by a local eatery through an ECO like Swiggy?
quiz.why: Under Section 9(5), the ECO is liable to pay GST on notified restaurant services supplied through its platform.

quiz.q: What must an ECO do if it has no physical presence or representative in the taxable territory?
o: Appoint a person in taxable territory
quiz.why: Under Section 9(5) provisos, the ECO must appoint a person in the taxable territory for the purpose of paying tax.

topics.title: Classification of Goods and Services and Rate Structure
topics.section: Customs Tariff Act 1975, HSN / Chapter 99 Scheme
explain: Classification determines the applicable tax rate by identifying chapter, heading, sub-heading, and tariff item.
Goods classification is based on the 8-digit HSN code under the First Schedule to Customs Tariff Act, 1975.
Services classification follows the Scheme of Classification of Services under Chapter 99 (Sections 5 to 9).
Broad CGST rates for services: 0.75%, 2.5%, 3.75%, 9%, 20% (IGST rates: 1.5%, 5%, 7.5%, 18%, 40%).
Real Estate: Affordable housing @ 1% effective GST without ITC; Non-affordable/RREP commercial @ 5% effective GST without ITC (requires 80% inputs from registered persons).
topics.example: A product is matched to its 8-digit HSN code in the Customs Tariff Schedule to determine whether it falls under the 5%, 12%, 18%, or 28% GST rate band.
remember: Chapter 99 is specifically reserved for classification of services.
Real estate concessional rates (1% and 5%) require purchasing at least 80% inputs/input services from registered persons.
mistakes: Assuming real estate developers can claim Input Tax Credit on 1% or 5% concessional rates.
Confusing goods HSN codes with service codes under Chapter 99.

quiz.q: Which Chapter number is assigned for the classification of services under GST?
quiz.why: Chapter 99 of the Scheme of Classification of Services is assigned for classifying services under GST.

quiz.q: What is the effective GST rate without ITC for construction of affordable housing in new real estate projects?
quiz.why: Promoters pay effective 1% GST without ITC on construction of affordable housing projects.

topics.title: Composition Levy
explain: Composition scheme is an optional simplified scheme for small taxpayers to lower tax rates and compliance costs.

Eligibility under Sec 10(1) & 10(2): Preceding FY aggregate turnover <= Rs 1.5 Crore (Rs 75 Lakhs for 8 Special Category States: Arunachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, Tripura).

Tax Rates under 10(1): Manufacturers pay 1% (0.5% CGST + 0.5% SGST) of turnover in State/UT; Restaurants pay 5% (2.5% CGST + 2.5% SGST) of turnover in State/UT; Traders pay 1% (0.5% CGST + 0.5% SGST) of TAXABLE turnover in State/UT.

Marginal Service under 10(1): Composition suppliers of goods/restaurants can supply other services up to 10% of preceding FY turnover in State/UT or Rs 5 Lakhs, whichever is higher (interest on loans/deposits excluded).
Eligibility under Sec 10(2A): Service providers with preceding FY aggregate turnover <= Rs 50 Lakhs can pay tax @ 6% (3% CGST + 3% SGST) of turnover in State/UT.

Ineligible persons: Manufacturers of ice cream, pan masala, tobacco, aerated waters, fly ash bricks/blocks, building bricks, earthen/roofing tiles; inter-State outward suppliers; ECO service suppliers under Sec 52; casual or non-resident taxable persons; non-taxable goods suppliers.
Key Conditions: Cannot collect tax from buyers, cannot claim ITC, must issue Bill of Supply instead of Tax Invoice, option applies uniformly to all GSTINs under the same PAN.

flow.title: Checking Eligibility for Composition Scheme under Section 10(1)
steps: Adopt scheme for all PAN entities
Pay flat rate and issue Bill of Supply

topics.example: A retail trader in Maharashtra with Rs 80 Lakhs turnover in the preceding year pays flat 1% tax on taxable turnover and issues Bills of Supply without charging GST to customers.
remember: Traders pay 1% tax on TAXABLE turnover in State, whereas Manufacturers and Restaurants pay on TOTAL turnover in State.
Composition taxpayers cannot claim ITC and cannot collect tax from customers.
mistakes: Thinking a composition taxpayer can make inter-State outward supplies of goods or services.
Applying composition scheme to one business place while keeping another business place under normal scheme on the same PAN.

quiz.q: What is the aggregate turnover limit in the preceding financial year for opting composition scheme under Section 10(1) in Special Category State Mizoram?
quiz.why: For 8 special category states including Mizoram, the threshold turnover limit is Rs 75 Lakhs.

quiz.q: What is the tax rate applicable for a salon owner opting for composition scheme under Section 10(2A)?
quiz.why: Section 10(2A) prescribes a tax rate of 6% (3% CGST + 3% SGST/UTGST) for eligible service providers.
